review_note: No specific unresolved intervention pressure was evident. Revenue rose 23%, gross margin improved 80bps to 57.2%, adjusted EBITDA increased fourfold, loss before tax halved, cash was £20.6m and contracted activity provided strong revenue visibility, supplying multiple strong quantified contrary indicators.

COVID disruption reduced revenue 21%, widened the adjusted EBITDA loss, prompted practical cost reductions and additional debt funding, and produced a downside scenario involving a bank-covenant breach. Gross margin improved 110bps, loss before tax reduced materially, cash remained £15.6m, second-half revenue recovered 26% and more than 75% of forecast revenue was visible, supplying meaningful contrary evidence.

The Group remained loss-making, had only £1.1m cash after a £4.0m decline, was replacing an expiring revolving facility and identified sufficient funding until sustained cash generation as its key financial risk. Revenue nevertheless rose 44% to a record, gross margin expanded 490bps to 51.6%, cost control produced positive second-half adjusted EBITDA and forecast revenue visibility was strong, supplying substantial contrary evidence.

Rail-project delays drove a 30% revenue decline, a 91% fall in underlying operating profit and a 310bps gross-margin contraction, indicating substantial operating pressure despite cost-base flexibility. Net debt rose modestly, while order intake increased 34%, the order book grew 52% and the balance sheet remained described as strong, supplying meaningful contrary evidence.

Around £8m of expected revenue was deferred, revenue fell 12%, gross margin contracted 240bps, the Group moved to an operating loss and its bank agreed to remove the debt-service covenant for the year. Net debt fell 38%, order intake strengthened and the order book reached a record £27.3m, supplying meaningful but not decisive contrary evidence.

A small underlying operating loss and continuing dependence on project timing and renewed bank facilities supplied contained pressure; gross margin slipped 20bps and net debt increased but remained modest. Revenue rose 12%, the loss narrowed, operating cash flow was positive and the order book grew 14% to £31.6m, supplying strong quantified contrary evidence.
